name: Eaton House
use: Former mini-dorm (50 students), arts theme; part of the four-building Minis
style: Two-storey wood-frame houses with vertical board siding and gabled roofs (from photos)
statusNote: Minis closed at the end of spring 2026; future not announced

facts.text: Dedicated October 17, 1976 as a residence and learning community for creative-arts students; named for Forrest M. Eaton (class of 1926), trustee chair 1959-67.

Housing's Minis pages (archived April 2026) state the Minis were expected to close permanently at the end of the spring 2026 semester and were not available for 2026-27 assignments; the live pages now return "Access denied" and the Minis are absent from the current residence-hall list.

Housing described Eaton (50 students, The Arts theme, singles and doubles) as a small, eclectic arts community on the quieter side of campus near College Woods. The four Minis (Eaton, Hall, Marston, Richardson) functioned as one hall; residents could swipe into all four.
Accessibility per Housing: limited-use bathrooms, roll-in building access, strobe alerts in some rooms; gender-inclusive restrooms. No elevator or AC listed.

In February 2021 about 20 residents were moved out so Eaton could serve as back-up COVID-19 quarantine housing; Housing called it the least-populated residential community with an ideal layout for that use.

verdict: One of the 1976 'Minis', a weathered board-clad cabin dorm in the pines, closed in 2026.
notes: Reference photos show the Minis as low two-storey wood-frame buildings clad in grey vertical boards, with gabled roofs, exterior stairs and decks, set among tall pines near College Woods; modest, cabin-like, weathered. Archives photo (historic): long two-storey gabled wood buildings on open lawn. Archived Housing images for Eaton failed to download from the Internet Archive. No licensed photo found.
judgeNotes: Reference photos show modest grey wood-frame buildings. Function low because it is closed. Down about a point from the old run, which still had the Minis in use.
